_README: Repairs for the ONE class of text-layer corruption that is not algorithmically
recoverable: a conjunct whose second consonant was never mapped, so the
character is simply absent (ग्राम -> ग्ाम). The signature is a halant followed
by a dependent vowel, detected by textnorm.has_dropped_consonant().
Across all 190 pages this is 657 occurrences but only 73 distinct tokens, so a
hand-verified map is tractable and fully auditable — no model, no guessing at
runtime. Most are a missing rakar र; the rest are missing ष, ञ, व, य, ण.
Every entry was read in context. Ambiguous ones are noted in _NOTES.
Regenerate the candidate list with:  scripts/find_conjunct_gaps.py

_NOTES.क्ा: = कक्षा, confirmed in context ('मेरी कक्षा में _____ विद्यार्थी हैं', p10). Not क्या: real क्या survives extraction intact.
_NOTES.घ्ा: NOT a dropped consonant — it is the list marker (घ) with a spurious matra. Appears in क/ख/ग/घ enumerations.
_NOTES.ग्ा: = ग्रा, from the abbreviation 'कि.ग्रा.' and from किलोग्राम split across spans.
_NOTES.साग्ेस: = साग्रेस (Sagres, Portugal), the far end of the Talon-Sagres road route in ch4/ch5.
_NOTES.श्ेण्ाु: LOW CONFIDENCE. A shopkeeper's given name on p106; read as श्रेणु. Single occurrence.
_NOTES.क्षा: = कक्षा. A SECOND corruption class: a dropped LEADING letter, which has no halant+vowel signature and so is invisible to has_dropped_consonant(). Found by scanning short frequent tokens for non-words. 27 occurrences.
_NOTES.क्ष: = कक्ष (room), same dropped-leading-letter class. Context: 'कक्षाओं के लिए कितने कक्ष हैं' (p10). 12 occurrences.
